hypothesis: For Array inputs, replacing the `for await (const raw of handle)` chunk iteration in LineIndex.build with a plain index-based `for` loop (inside the same async build, same locals, no extracted function, no state object) removes the per-chunk async-from-sync-iterator wrapping and microtask hop, and that change alone measurably affects the sealed benchmark's speedup. Non-array inputs keep `for await` unchanged. Single change: input iteration shape only.

steps.change: In `static async build` (L215-343), directly after `const started = performance.now();` (L239) and before the `for await` line (L241), insert exactly: `const arr = Array.isArray(handle) ? (handle as ReadonlyArray<Buffer | string>) : undefined;` with a one-line comment above it: `// 数组输入：按下标同步遍历（不经 async-from-sync 迭代器）；其余输入仍走 for await。` Do NOT narrow or reassign `handle`; the else branch keeps iterating the original `handle` with its original union type.

Take the current per-chunk body, i.e. the statements currently inside the `for await` braces from L242 (`const buf: Buffer = typeof raw === 'string' ? Buffer.from(raw) : (raw as Buffer);`) through L300 (the closing `}` of the `if (onProgress && totalBytes - lastReport >= reportInterval) { ... }` block). Call this BODY. BODY must be copied character-for-character into both branches below: same byte-wise `for (let i = 0; i < n; i++)` loop, same inString/escaped handling at L247-251, same switch cases, same `line % interval === 0` checks, same two `recordEndLines.push` / `recordEndOffsets.push(chunkBase + i + 1)` pushes, same `const chunkBase = totalBytes;` before the byte loop, same `totalBytes += n;` after it, and same onProgress block (`lastReport = totalBytes; onProgress({ bytesRead: totalBytes, lines: line, done: false });`). No edits, no reordering, no helper function, no closure.

Replace the whole statement `for await (const raw of handle) { BODY }` (L241-301) with: `if (arr !== undefined) { for (let ci = 0; ci < arr.length; ci++) { const raw = arr[ci] as Buffer | string; BODY } } else { for await (const raw of handle) { BODY } }`. Use the live `arr.length` in the loop condition (not a cached length) so iteration count matches the array iterator used by for-await. The variable name inside both loops stays `raw` so BODY is unchanged. Everything from `const eof = true;` (L303) to the end of build stays exactly as it is, outside the if/else.

Leave everything else alone: no change to the string scanner, the `line % interval` checkpoint logic (no nextCp), record storage, the EOF tail handling, the final `onProgress({ ..., done: true })`, buildMs timing, the LineIndex constructor call, or any other method. Semantics preserved by construction: string chunks still go through `Buffer.from(raw)` in BODY; onProgress still fires after each chunk once `totalBytes - lastReport >= reportInterval`, in the same order with the same values; totalBytes/chunkBase accounting is identical because BODY is identical; Readable streams, async iterables and non-array sync iterables (e.g. generators, Sets) take the untouched `for await` path, so their iterator close-on-throw behavior is unchanged. Known non-observable difference for arrays: no per-chunk await/microtask hop (and elements are not awaited, which only matters for Promise elements, outside the declared `Buffer | string` element type); arrays have no iterator `return()`, so throw-from-onProgress behavior is identical.

Verify: run `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm test` (all of src/indexer/__tests__ and src/perf/__tests__ must pass), then the sealed `node scripts/benchmark-index-build.mjs` at least 3 times and report each primary score plus the median. Before benchmarking, confirm via `git diff` that the two BODY copies are identical to each other and to the original L242-300 (e.g. extract both branches and diff them).

expected_outcome.estimated_impact: ~0% (expected score ~0.85-0.95 vs baseline 0.898; within the ±0.05-0.08 noise band)
expected_outcome.rationale: Honest expectation is a null result. The research brief measured this exact change in scratch (candidate d2 'asyncArr index loop') at 0.882/0.804/0.923 vs a current-code mirror of 0.818/0.908/0.793, and a full sync duplicate (d1) was also neutral, as was round 1's sync scanChunk kernel (0.897). The benchmark feeds ~16 chunks per build, so per-chunk async iterator overhead is a few microseconds against a ~30 ms build; the per-byte loop body (75% of bytes inside strings) dominates. This plan exists to satisfy H003 with the infrastructure family and to confirm, under the sealed benchmark and with a strictly single change, that chunk iteration shape is not a lever. A score outside 0.85-0.95 would be noteworthy and worth re-running.

sub_score_expectations.cur_median_mb_s: roughly unchanged vs round-1 values (~500-570 MB/s, noise-dominated)

history_reference.builds_on: Research brief round_2 idea 'Index-based loop for Array inputs inside the existing async build' (approach_family infrastructure); round_1 lesson that state must stay in locals.
history_reference.avoids: Round-1 plan B pattern (sync scanChunk kernel with ScanState marshaling, 0.897); any function extraction or state object; bundling a second change (round-1 plans A and C rejected under H001); touching the string scanner, nextCp, or record storage (left to other planners / later rounds); brief DO NOT items: lazy record storage, hasFirst guard, Uint8Array table in strings, 8x unroll, Buffer#indexOf skipping.
